messages:
mike_sales: Heads-up — FinServCo just pushed a draft MSA that includes a few product asks we need to triage: 99.99% uptime SLA, p99 < 50ms for short-text generation, and 24/7 phone support with <30min response for Sev1. They want this in the contract to close an enterprise deal. Can product advise on feasibility and routing?

jess_support: Thanks Mike. Logged initial intake: customer id FS-9843. Quick notes from support call: traffic will be bursty (batch windows end of day), model is our standard chat generation. They flagged compliance requirements too.

anna_product: Quick take — 99.99% and 50ms p99 are both aggressive for hosted by-default. We need to confirm deployment mode (hosted vs Dedicated) and if they expect single-region or multi-region failover. Also need to check whether their traffic pattern can be smoothed or requires reserved capacity.

sam_eng: If they require p99 50ms we should assume Dedicated with pinned capacity + regional failover. Cost delta is large. Also need to know sequence length distribution — 50ms is plausible for short prompts (~<=128 tokens) on V100/A100-sized configs but not for long contexts.

ria_pm: Suggest fast-path triage: 1) get traffic profile (RPS, seq length, concurrency), 2) decide deployment target (Hosted SLA vs Dedicated contract), 3) SLO spec doc and runbook, 4) route to SLA intake epic. I can own the intake doc if we agree.

mike_sales: They told me avg RPS ~20 with spikes to 500 for 5–10m windows, avg seq len 60 tokens. Willing to consider Dedicated if pricing is reasonable. They want the SLA baked into the MSA by EOW.

jess_support: Noted. Risk flags: bursty spikes mean autoscaling warm-up could cause transient p99 violations. Also support ask for 24/7 phone — we need to confirm on-call burn/rotation and what support tier they expect.

anna_product: Actionable next steps: - create a Jira SLA intake ticket with {customer, traffic profile, required SLOs, desired support tier} - engineering to give capacity/latency feasibility and suggested configs - sales ops to draft contract clauses (targets, credits, failure modes). Who owns the Jira?

sam_eng: I'll pair with oncall to run a quick perf estimate. For initial answer we can provide two options: (A) Hosted SLA w/ regional redundancy: 99.95% and p99 ~70–120ms depending on model; (B) Dedicated reserved capacity + multi-AZ: 99.99% and p99 ~40–60ms for short prompts. Need exact model + quantization level.

oncall-bot: Incident playbook link: https://confluence.redwood/ops/sla-sre-playbook — includes escalation routing, contact matrix, and phone handoff steps.

ria_pm: I'll open the intake ticket and set labels `sla-intake`, `enterprise`, `fastpath`. Assign to @anna_product for scope and @sam_eng for feasibility. Also schedule 30m sync with FinServCo + Solutions Eng tomorrow.

mike_sales: Perfect — please cc sales-ops on the ticket. I'll send the customer a tentative SLA options doc. If we can scope the Dedicated pricing quickly we can get this signed. :thumbsup:

anna_product: Sounds good. One more note — include rollback/fallback policy in the MSA: automatic fallback to lower-tier model in overload and clear credit/measurement method. We'll also require a monitoring tag to surface SLO violations to customer portal.

ria_pm: Ticket created: https://jira.redwood/browse/RI-SLA-1324 — assigned. Closing loop here, will update as we get eng estimates.

mike_sales: Thanks all. Keep me posted, customer expects answer by EOD Friday.
